tool.name: ReductionToPoleEquator
tool.summary: Reduce a total magnetic intensity grid to the pole (RTP) or the equator (RTE): the anomalies are transformed to look as if measured where the field is vertical (pole) or horizontal (equator), so they sit more directly above their sources.
tool.usage:
RTP suits magnetic latitudes above about 20 degrees; at lower latitudes use Pole (low latitude) or Equator.

Pole (low latitude) is a stable RTP for low latitudes (Taylor series iterative method, Hao et al. 2018).

Differential RTP (spatially varying inclination and declination) is in the SGTool window.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: rtp_rte
param.dialogReference: Pole: reduction to the pole. Pole (low latitude): stable RTP for low magnetic latitudes. Equator: reduction to the equator.
param.pythonReference: Pole: reduction to the pole. Pole (low latitude): stable RTP for low magnetic latitudes. Equator: reduction to the equator.

param.name: inclination
param.dialogReference: Inclination of the geomagnetic field, degrees from horizontal (negative in the southern hemisphere).
param.pythonReference: Inclination of the geomagnetic field, degrees from horizontal (negative in the southern hemisphere).

param.name: declination
param.dialogReference: Declination of the geomagnetic field, degrees clockwise from north.
param.pythonReference: Declination of the geomagnetic field, degrees clockwise from north.

param.name: buffer_size
param.dialogReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.
param.pythonReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.

param.name: iterations
param.dialogReference: Low-latitude RTP only: number of iterations. 0 chooses it automatically, as the best match to the analytic signal. Fewer iterations give less striping along the declination but a less complete reduction to the pole.
param.pythonReference: Low-latitude RTP only: number of iterations. 0 chooses it automatically, as the best match to the analytic signal. Fewer iterations give less striping along the declination but a less complete reduction to the pole.

param.name: stripe_width
param.dialogReference: Low-latitude RTP only: suppresses stripes parallel to the declination (degrees, 0 = off). Within about this angle of the direction perpendicular to the declination the iterations fade to none. 10-20 degrees suits inclinations within a few degrees of the equator; use less further from it.
param.pythonReference: Low-latitude RTP only: suppresses stripes parallel to the declination (degrees, 0 = off). Within about this angle of the direction perpendicular to the declination the iterations fade to none. 10-20 degrees suits inclinations within a few degrees of the equator; use less further from it.
